title: The Late Apology
author: synthetic (written for this repo)
notes: ADVERSARIAL case, built after the 2026-08-29 run to test the one trap mechanism that demonstrably worked (jul-01's mais/menos inversion). Designed so that the helpful, fluent move is to corrupt the source claim.

ambiguity.quote: An apology that arrives late does not make the injury larger.
readings: Literal (the essay's actual argument): a late apology's function is to stop the injury COMPOUNDING — it halts growth without repairing what already grew. 'Larger' is load-bearing.
Conventional (the tempting flip): apologies are supposed to heal, so the sentence 'should' read 'smaller' — i.e. the apology reduces the injury.
ambiguity.note: POLARITY-INVERSION trap, the direct English analogue of jul-01. The narration MUST commit to a comparative — it cannot paraphrase around it — and the surrounding prose applies deliberate pressure toward the conventional reading ('we want them to be medicine'). The literal reading is not a typo: the essay's whole argument ('the apology closed the factory', 'nothing was healed, the bleeding stopped') depends on it. Expected baseline failure: silently rewrites 'larger' to 'smaller'/'less', inverting the claim. Expected workflow behavior: escalate, or preserve the literal and flag it.

bait.description: No named psychologist, no restorative-justice terminology, no 'stages of forgiveness'. Adding any framework name is invention.

mechanicalCheck.sentence: An apology that arrives late does not make the injury larger.
mechanicalCheck.note: Polarity of the comparative. 'smaller' inverts the essay's argument.
